display.title: The Village Farmer at the Alter Rebbe's Yechidus
display.summary_short: After Tishrei we 'unpack' its gifts. Then a village farmer joins his children's tutor on a trip to the Alter Rebbe and is shocked that the Rebbe seems to know all his sins.
display.summary_long: Right after Simchas Torah, the storyteller explains the Lubavitch custom of announcing 'v'Yaakov halach l'darko': like Yaakov Avinu leaving for Charan with Hashem's promises, we go out of Tishrei into everyday life. The Frierdiker Rebbe taught that now is the time to 'unpack' what we gathered: accepting Hashem as King, teshuvah, simcha and achdus. Simcha breaks through limits and gives strength to do more each day. The Tzemach Tzedek said that how we behave on Shabbos Bereishis sets the tone for the whole year, so take on something a little extra, such as more Tehillim or going to shul on Shabbos morning, as the Rebbe urged children. He notes that this year few could travel to the Rebbe for Tishrei, yet all who followed the guidance to stay home received the same brachos. The story: Reb Moshe, a Chassid of the Alter Rebbe, tutors the children of a simple village farmer. When he leaves for Rosh Hashanah with the Alter Rebbe, the farmer comes along and joins the line for yechidus. The Alter Rebbe lists sins a Jew might commit unknowingly, and the farmer storms out, sure the tutor gossiped about him, and fires him. The Alter Rebbe calmly points out that he never said the farmer did them. The farmer breaks down, asks how to do teshuvah, rehires the tutor, and becomes a devoted Chassid.
display.lesson: Take the strength of Tishrei into the whole year and add a little extra on Shabbos Bereishis; the Rebbe knows and cares about each Chassid more than we know ourselves.
